title: candidate-gradient-notes-luca-moreno
content:
Quick overnight scratchpad after loop with candidate (Aisha Patel) — my immediate impressions and follow-ups.

Context: loop included 45m system-design + 30m coding (pairing on a simplified KV cache eviction problem) + 15m culture/behavioural. Candidate has recent infra experience at a mid-stage company with model-serving exposure, but not deep low-level kernel/quantization work.

What surprised me
- Thoughtful about request routing and cost tiers: sketched a policy graph that mapped routes to capacity pools, liked the idea of soft fallbacks. Shows good product-awareness.
- Fractured mental model around batching. They treat batching purely as throughput optimization and didn't discuss latency SLO tradeoffs or caching interactions (prefix/KV). This is a noticeable gap for an inference-runtime role.

Coding exercise notes
- Implemented a basic LRU/TTL hybrid in Python. Correctness mostly fine, but missed edge-cases around concurrent evictions (race on size constraints).
- Paired well, responded to hints; however when pushed on making it lock-free they defaulted to coarse locks rather than exploring lock striping or optimistic approaches.
- Time management: spent ~10m on micro-optimizations that weren't relevant to the prompt; missed opportunity to discuss tradeoffs faster.

System design thread
- Good high-level decomposition: router, pool manager, health-checker, policy engine. Brought up real concerns re: KV cache invalidation on model rollouts — strong practical instincts.
- Sketch lacked metrics/observability specifics: where would you export per-prefix hit rate, how to set cache TTLs by model? They gave plausible answers but not concrete signal types.

Culture / team fit
- Collaborative tone, asked clarifying questions, receptive to feedback.
- Mentorship examples were junior-leaning; hasn't led cross-functional rollout of infra/features yet.

Risks
- Lacks low-level inference optimizations experience (quantization kernels, ATen/TVM exposure). Hard to get them up to speed quickly for a role requiring kernel-level tweaks.
- Concurrency/race conditions: showed limited pattern depth for lock-free designs under high throughput. Potential SRE friction during incidents.

Signals in favor
- Strong product intuition for routing/cost tiers, could be effective on the Smart Routing/team facing policy layer (less kernel-focused).
- Fast learner, demonstrated when paired; could own features that bridge infra and product (e.g., autoscaling policy UX).

Calibration suggestion
- Recommend for a Platform Engineer II role focused on policy/routing/observability rather than low-level runtime maintainer. If we consider them for the runtime team, hiring manager should accept a 3-4 month ramp plan and pair them with a senior runtime engineer on kernel topics.

Action items / follow-ups
- Ask hiring manager (Marcus) if we have an open policy/routing slot or would prefer hiring for kernel skillset. (Slack: #hiring-runtime thread pinned, see message ts 2026-03-03T09:12).
- If moving forward, request a short take-home focused on concurrent caching (simulate multiple writers/readers + eviction) to probe lock-free/optimistic strategies.
- Share this note with Anika and Marcus for calibration; capture final recommendation in Greenhouse.

Open questions to resolve before panel vote
- Does the hiring ladder value product-forward runtime engineers (policy/orchestration) equally to kernel/quantization folks? Needs hiring rubric clarification (see CONFLUENCE-rtg-ladders).
- What compensation band would we offer for a Platform Engineer II vs Senior Runtime Engineer — will affect acceptance given candidate's current comp.

Personal gut summary (short)
- Candidate: solid, practical, good communicator. Not ideal for low-level runtime maintainer. High chance to succeed in a policy/routing/observability domain after a short ramp.

Notes to self: save example sketch and pair session recording to linked_artifacts if GH PR emerges. During debrief, emphasize concurrency examples vs kernel examples to align expectations.

End of notes.
